finding.claim: POST /checkout computes the charge total from client-supplied item price and qty, with no server-side catalog lookup or validation. An authenticated user can send price 0.01 or a negative price or qty and pay almost nothing, or get a negative charge (a refund-like credit) while the order is still accepted.
finding.sink: req.payments.charge(req.user.id, total) at cart.js:6, and the charged total returned at cart.js:7

trace.note: total = sum of i.price * i.qty, both taken straight from the request body
the attacker-computed total is passed to payments.charge with no recomputation
the response echoes the charged amount

finding.guards_checked: No price lookup, no check for negative, zero, fractional or non-numeric values, and no minimum total. The safer /checkout-v2 route in the same file shows the intended server-side pricing, but /checkout remains mounted and reachable. No auth middleware is visible in this file, so req.user is assumed to be set upstream. The attack only needs any logged-in user.

verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums req.body price*qty with no catalog lookup or range check, cart.js:6 charges that total and cart.js:7 echoes it, while only /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13-14) prices server-side. Only cart.js exists, so no upstream validation is visible; the attacker only needs to be a logged-in user, and req.user is assumed to be set upstream.
